Title: Dynamic lumbopelvic stabilization for treatment of stress urinary incontinence in women: Controlled and randomized clinical trial
Author: de Souza Abreu et al.
Comment: Table 3 reports separate King’s Health Questionnaire domains and no total score. Per the one-row-per-effect rule, the Impact of incontinence domain was selected as the closest direct measure of incontinence-related life impact. The reported P = 0.003 is an interaction P value across the 2 × 3 repeated-measures analysis and is not a simple post-treatment between-group P value, so it was not entered in p_value. M_diff was not computed because the study used a multi-factor repeated-measures ANOVA. Higher raw King’s Health Questionnaire domain scores appear to reflect worse quality of life from the observed interpretation, but the supplied paper text does not explicitly state scoring direction or scale range; no direction transformation or range was recorded.
Design Type: Controlled randomized parallel blinded clinical trial with repeated measures
Study Environment: Public gynecological care service; individually supervised exercise sessions plus daily home exercise
Medium: In-person supervised exercise and home exercise
Content length: 10 supervised sessions over 5 weeks, approximately 30 min each, plus daily home exercise
Topic of Content: Dynamic lumbopelvic stabilization added to pelvic floor muscle strengthening
Participant type: Women aged 18 years or older with self-reported urinary loss and a positive cough-provocation test
Outcome measurement: King’s Health Questionnaire – Impact of incontinence domain, post-test
Outcome variable: Incontinence-related quality of life (King’s Health Questionnaire – Impact of incontinence domain)
effect_direction: favors combined indirect training plus PFMT

Title: Effect of Combined Pallof Press and Kegels Training for Urinary Incontinence in Multigravida Women and Quality of Life
Author: Pinky Maria Jose; R.V Vijaya Kumar
Comment: The direct post-test mean difference was computed as treatment minus control: 4.66 - 4.8 = -0.14; SE_diff was computed from the two explicitly reported post-test SDs and n=15 per group. Hedges g=0.213 was computed from the post-test means, SDs, and group sizes and reverse-signed because lower IIQ-7 scores represent better quality of life, so positive g favors combined Kegel + Pallof treatment. No direct between-group inferential statistic is clearly reported. The displayed Wilcoxon statistics are within-group pretest-post-test tests and were therefore not attached to this between-group result. Table 2 gives the combined group's post-test IIQ-7 SD as 0.61, whereas the following prose gives 0.16; the table value was used because the targeted result location is the tabulated post-test estimate. The abstract says the IIQ-7 critical value was not significant, conflicting with the Results narrative's claim of a significantly greater improvement.
Design Type: Simple experimental two-group pretest-posttest intervention study with random grouping stated by the authors
domain: Urinary incontinence rehabilitation and incontinence-related quality of life
Study Environment: Physiotherapy clinics and houses in and around Bangalore
Medium: Exercise intervention delivered daily for 8 weeks
Topic of Content: Kegel pelvic floor muscle training with or without Pallof press core/trunk exercise
Participant type: Multigravida women aged 30-40 years with urinary incontinence
effect_direction: favors combined indirect training plus PFMT

Title: Paula method of circular muscle exercises for urinary stress incontinence—a clinical trial
Author: Liebergall-Wischnitzer et al.
Comment: The paper reports only arm-specific within-group changes and p values; it explicitly states that the pilot was designed for within-group, not between-group, effects. No inferential between-group comparison was reported. M_diff was computed as 8.6 - (-4.6) = 13.2 points, SE_diff as sqrt(69.0^2/29 + 18.8^2/30) = 13.26, and Hedges g as approximately 0.26 from the reported change-score means, SDs, and analyzed group sizes. The reported arm-specific p values (0.7 and 0.02) were not entered as a between-group p value. Although the paper says the possible total is 110 points, it does not explicitly state the scale minimum, so outcome_scale_min and outcome_scale_max are left null.
